analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance (formerly Suven Pharma) is a business in clear multi-year earnings decline being priced as a high-growth compounder — EV/EBITDA of 94.7x for a company whose net profit has fallen from INR 454 Cr in FY22 to INR 265 Cr in FY25 is disconnected from reality. The sudden near-tripling of total assets in FY25 (INR 2,254 Cr to INR 5,568 Cr) and jump in borrowings to INR 451 Cr signal a large acquisition whose returns are entirely unproven.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 57.49% provides adequate governance confidence
OCF has been positive in all 5 years, indicating the underlying business does convert earnings to cash
Gross margin of 71.5% reflects the value-add in CDMO/API synthesis
key_risks: Net profit in a confirmed 3-year decline: INR 454 Cr (FY22) → INR 411 Cr → INR 300 Cr → INR 265 Cr (FY25)
EV/EBITDA of 94.7x is unjustifiable for any business, let alone a declining one — the market is pricing in a complete earnings reversal
Operating margin of only 8.89% for a supposedly specialty pharma/CDMO company is far too thin
red_flags: Total assets nearly tripled in FY25 (INR 2,254 Cr to INR 5,568 Cr) with borrowings jumping from INR 65 Cr to INR 451 Cr — a large unproven acquisition
Company rebranded from Suven Pharmaceuticals to Cohance in May 2025 — name changes during earnings stress are a governance caution signal for me
FCF declining steadily: INR 304 Cr (FY20) → INR 132 Cr (FY25) even as net profit was much higher in prior years
analysis.detailed_analysis: I have a simple rule: I do not pay 94x EBITDA for a business whose profits have been falling for three consecutive years. The CDMO/contract pharma model can be excellent, but Cohance's operating margin of 8.89% tells me this is not yet a differentiated, high-value CDMO — it is still largely a commodity chemicals and API manufacturer. The sudden balance sheet expansion in FY25 with debt funding an acquisition is precisely the kind of aggressive move I avoid; I need to see at least two to three years of evidence that any acquisition earns its cost of capital.
